newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens on ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens on ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in moderate early trading on Thursday on the back of ample liquidity, dealers said.
They said operators were a bit worried at the opening, one day after a new bank reserve requirement rate became effective, but adequate supply helped calm the market.
A five percent reserve rate was made effective on Wednesday.
Overnight money fell to 10.0/10.5 percent from 14.0 percent and overnight swap was down to 0.9/1.1 from 1.5 points.
One local bank dealer said flush rupiah supply led players to go slightly long on dollars due to the extended weekend.

"I think people prefer to be a bit long on dollars because we don't know what would happen through the weekend," he said, adding operators were cautious due to the heated political climate six weeks before the May 29 general elections.
Spot rupiah was at 2,409.0/09.5 at 0230 GMT against an opening of 2,407.75/08.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,408.85/09.10 and 2,407.65/08.50, respectively.
"There is not much activity this morning. There are some worries about liquidity but I think some people are just holding back for a while," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said longer-term rates were stable in slow trade.
One-month swaps were at 11.25/12.00, two at 23.25/24.50, three at 34.5/35.0 and six at 71.0/72.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band at 2,401/2,449 on Wednesday.
The market will be closed on Friday for a Moslem festival and will reopen on Monday.
